items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: This same thing applies to Little Louie. Little Louie heard the records of the original Dixieland Jazz Band, but I can tell you he never heard Bowling play. ... Little Louie, the man I'm talking about is Louis Armstrong

ctx.x: Before who was this came to be?

I mean Clarence Williams. You got me right that time because I'm making a mistake. I'm just telling you, I'm reading. I'm not reading. I'm telling you from my mind. Clarence Williams came to New York around 1923. The first white man he met on Broadway was me with an introduction from A.J. Perron, which you'll find in their books too. And this Negro is supposed to have her buddy bowling play. Now let me tell you about this man, who he is, where he come from. If any of you serious scholars doubt me, I was just…

All right. This is a letter dated May the 27th, 1958 from Don Fowler, 9441 Southwest 8th Drive, Portland 1, Oregon. It's to D. James, D. James, Nick LaRocca, at 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans, 13, Louisiana. And here's a paragraph that Mr. LaRocca would like for me to read. The other day I ran across an interesting statement by Louis Armstrong in his book, Satchmo. He is discussing his life in New Orleans in 1918, and this is a paragraph.
